verdict.rationale: The only evidence of event-driven automation is AWS Budgets. A user sets a budget with actual or forecasted spend thresholds, and AWS can then automatically apply an IAM policy that blocks new resource provisioning. That is a genuine rule-triggers-action capability, but it is limited to cost events, and the pack documents no general event bus or rule engine. Missing for 10: general-purpose event rules across services, event-to-target routing (e.g. invoking Lambda on events), any documentation beyond budget actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can use AWS Budgets to track and take action on your AWS costs and usage.
you could automatically apply a custom IAM policy that denies you the ability to provision additional resources within an account.
You can choose to be alerted for both actual (after accruing) and forecasted (before accruing) spends.
